# Complete the customer billing-schedule migration

Finish the service-to-customer migration for recurring billing. Creating a customer must create a monthly billing schedule only when that customer has an offering. When an existing customer gains or changes an `offeringId`, replace any previous billing schedule with a customer-level schedule; an already-missing old schedule is not an error. Preserve the authenticated subject and business ID in the scheduler configuration.

Billing jobs receive `businessID` on the scheduler record and `customerId` in `scheduleParameters`. Resolve the customer and its offering, derive the offering billing-cycle time range, call the existing usage-total invoice path with that exact customer and range, and persist a billing record containing the returned invoice ID. Report processing failures through the existing audit channel instead of leaving the queue job with a partially stored billing record.

Route billing scheduler emissions to `scheduler_billing_queue` with the `billingReport` consumer name. All non-billing measurements must continue to use the normal scheduler queue and their dimension consumer. Finally, a usage read for a customer without an offering should return an empty result rather than fail.

Verify with:

    cd /app && npm run build && npm run test:ci -- --runInBand

33: -   [Git](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-Installing-Git)

35: -   A good IDE (such as [VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/), or [WebStorm](https://www.jetbrains.com/webstorm/))
36: -   Helpful for command line navigation [z](https://facilecode.com/how-to-setup-z-jump-around/)

38: # Setup
39: 
40: 1. Configure AWS CLI. `aws configure`. See sample config below. Use _us-east-1_ as default region and _json_ as default output format.
41: 
42: ```bash
43: aws configure
44: AWS Access Key ID [None]: XXXXXXXXXXX
45: AWS Secret Access Key [None]: XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
46: Default region name [None]: us-east-1
47: Default output format [None]: json
48: ```
49: 
50: 2. Clone the repository.
51: 3. Run: `npm run setup:influx` Visit _http://localhost:8086_ to make sure InfluxDB is running locally.
52: 4. Going through the setup guide of local InfuxDB. Configure the `test-usage-data` bucket, the `test-config` bucket and the `paigo` org. **Case sensitive**.
53: 5. [Get an API Token from the Influx instance](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/cloud/security/tokens/create-token/)
54: 6. Create the following file at the root directory of the project named `.env`, where the `INFLUX_URL`, `INFLUX_TOKEN` and `INFLUX_ORG` values are stored
55: 
56: Your token will be different than the one below.
57: 
58: ```txt
59: AUTH0_ISSUER_URL=https://auth.paigo.tech/
60: AUTH0_AUDIENCE=https://qnonyh1pc7.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
61: INFLUX_TOKEN=<fill_me_in>
62: INFLUX_ORG=paigo

65: STRIPE_TOKEN=<fill_me_in>

67: REDIS_PORT=6379
68: ```

70: 8. Navigate to the project folder you want to work on. Install dependencies. `npm ci`
71: 9. Run `npm run setup:redis`
72: 10. Run tests to ensure all tests passed. `npm run test`

74: ### Local Integration environment

Locally deployed will be a kind based kubernetes cluster, and then the paigo-backend docker image will be deployed into the kind cluster as a pod. The tests then run against that enviornment. This specifically is testing the `transformer` and `scheduler` functionality.

89: -   To run the api locally utilize `npm run build && npm run start:generic` with the appropriate values in via the `.env` file.
